findings.issue: ORDER BY clause built from unvalidated user-supplied sort string, enabling SQL injection
findings.evidence: getReviewsSorted does `ORDER BY ${sort}` with sort taken directly from req.query.sort in src/routes/api.ts (`const sort = (req.query.sort as string) || 'r.created_at DESC';`), with no whitelist — unlike getBooksPage, which whitelists via BOOK_SORT_COLUMNS.

findings.issue: Stored XSS: display_name and rating interpolated unescaped into raw HTML sent via res.send
findings.evidence: `${top.display_name} rated it ${top.rating}/5` — display_name is user-controlled with no sanitization at write time, and every other view in the app renders it through EJS `<%= %>` auto-escaping; this new route breaks that pattern.

findings.issue: Broken rating validation due to impossible AND condition, allowing out-of-range ratings to be persisted
findings.evidence: `if (!Number.isInteger(rating) || (rating < 1 && rating > 5))` — a number can't be both <1 and >5 simultaneously, so this clause is always false; ratings like 0, -5, or 99 pass validation and are written via Review.updateReview.

findings.issue: Off-by-one pagination offset skips the first page of results
findings.evidence: `OFFSET ?` is bound with `page * pageSize` instead of `(page - 1) * pageSize`; the caller defaults page to 1, so a default request for page 1 skips the first pageSize rows entirely, contradicting the comment 'page starts at 1'.
